classification.difficultyReason: Connect SSS and SAS proofs with corresponding sides, corresponding angles and supplementary angles to justify a perpendicular-bisector construction.

content.prompt: This question provides a proof of the construction of the perpendicular bisector of an interval. The arcs are of the same radius and centred at $A$ and $B$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2 construction diagram at upper right
spec.description: Equal-radius dashed construction arcs centred at A and B meet at P and Q. The supplied horizontal interval AB and vertical line PQ meet at M. No joining segments or right-angle marks are supplied.
spec.mathematics: A, M and B are collinear; P, M and Q are collinear. Both arcs have the same radius. Coordinates construct these relationships without supplying numerical measurements.

answer.worked: $AP=BP$ and $AQ=BQ$ because the construction arcs have equal radii. Also, $PQ=PQ$ (common side). Therefore $\triangle APQ\equiv\triangle BPQ$ (SSS).

answer.short: $\angle APQ=\angle BPQ$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked: From part b, $\triangle APQ\equiv\triangle BPQ$. Their matching angles at $P$ are equal, so $\angle APQ=\angle BPQ$.

answer.short: $AP=BP$, $\angle APM=\angle BPM$ and $PM=PM$, so $\triangle APM\equiv\triangle BPM$ (SAS).
answer.worked: $AP=BP$ (equal construction radii). Since $M$ lies on the ray $PQ$, part c gives $\angle APM=\angle BPM$. Also, $PM=PM$ (common side). The equal angles are included between the corresponding equal sides, so $\triangle APM\equiv\triangle BPM$ (SAS).

answer.short: $AM=BM$ by matching sides. The matching angles $\angle AMP$ and $\angle BMP$ are equal and sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$. Hence $PQ\perp AB$.
answer.worked:
From part d, matching sides give $AM=BM$, and matching angles give $\angle AMP=\angle BMP$. Since $A$, $M$ and $B$ lie on a straight line,
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AMP+\angle BMP&=180^\circ\\2\angle AMP&=180^\circ\\\angle AMP&=90^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $\angle BMP=90^\circ$ also. Since $P$, $M$ and $Q$ are collinear, $PQ\perp AB$.
